items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: Dick Cavett was looking at this, and he got just almost to that point, and he said, “I know where this is going, who did this?”

ctx.x: Yeah, I’ve learned that you’re quite a practical joker. Bob Rosengarden was saying, he called them “Wilderisms” that you used to do on the Dick Cavett band?

Oh yeah. I was always — you know the pages would ask the audience to write questions or some comment, make a comment about something. So he said, “why don’t you write something?” So I wrote a thing — I had been doing research on the Salem witch trials, and I discovered that during that period there were two sisters who were also burned at the stake — the Kendall sisters — and one was Mary and the other one was Susan Kendall. And it just turns out by coincidence that Mary Kendall was the first woman who burned at…
Wow. I wish we had a drum to go “titi-boom.”

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I did The Dick Cavett Show from the time it started until it went off the air.

ctx.x: Then you were on The Dick Cavett Show, weren’t you, for a long time?
I did The Dick Cavett Show from the time it started until it went off the air. And I used to do – at ABC, on radio, we also did The Merv Griffin Show, when he had his show on radio. We did that.
Was it different to play for radio and play for television? Would you be on camera sometimes for television?
